浜松餃子.summary: Fried in a circle in the pan and served with boiled bean sprouts in the middle. The light, cabbage-rich filling makes them easy to keep eating.
浜松餃子.tip: Eat them with the bean sprouts in the center to refresh your palate.

富士宮やきそば.summary: Firm, chewy steamed noodles topped with crispy pork bits (nikukasu) and sardine or mackerel powder (dashiko). Made famous by winning the B-1 Grand Prix.
富士宮やきそば.tip: Locals sprinkle plenty of dashiko on top. A perfect stop on a trip to see Mt. Fuji.

静岡おでん.summary: Oden simmered in a dark broth made with beef tendon, with every ingredient on a skewer. The grey kuro hanpen fish cake made from sardines or mackerel is a must.
静岡おでん.tip: Sprinkle on fish powder and green seaweed flakes. Try it at old-style candy shops or izakaya.

生しらす丼.summary: A rice bowl piled with raw whitebait caught in Suruga Bay. Freshness is everything, so it is best eaten in the fishing towns where it is landed.
生しらす丼.tip: Raw whitebait may not be served during the winter-to-spring closed season or on days when boats cannot go out.

三島コロッケ.summary: Croquettes made with Mishima-grown potatoes, known for their fluffy texture and natural sweetness. A local snack to eat while strolling.

浜名湖うな重.summary: Grilled eel over rice served in a lacquered box, from the area around Lake Hamana, a major center of eel farming.
浜名湖うな重.tip: Popular restaurants can sell out before noon, so go early.

サクラエビのかき揚げ.summary: A crispy fritter packed with sakura shrimp, which in Japan are landed only in Suruga Bay. Fragrant, crunchy and naturally sweet.
サクラエビのかき揚げ.tip: The fishing seasons are spring and autumn, when you can also try them raw or boiled.

金目の煮付け.summary: Splendid alfonsino, a red-skinned fish Izu is famous for, simmered in a sweet soy sauce glaze. The tender white flesh goes perfectly with rice.

とろろ汁.summary: Grated wild yam thinned with miso soup and poured over barley rice. A specialty of Mariko, an old post town on the Tokaido road.

山葵漬け.summary: Chopped wasabi pickled in sake lees, a Shizuoka specialty with a sharp kick. Great with rice, sashimi or fish cakes.

うなぎパイ.summary: Crispy pie cookies made with eel extract by Hamamatsu confectioner Shunkado. The classic Hamamatsu souvenir.
うなぎパイ.area: Hamamatsu and souvenir shops across the prefecture

安倍川もち.summary: Soft, freshly pounded rice cakes coated in roasted soybean flour (kinako) or smooth red bean paste, sold by teahouses along the Abe River for centuries.

こっこ.summary: A fluffy steamed sponge cake filled with milk cream, and one of Shizuoka's best-known souvenirs.
こっこ.area: Stations and souvenir shops across the prefecture

治一郎のバウムクーヘン.summary: A Hamamatsu-born baumkuchen loved for its moist texture. People travel from outside the prefecture to buy it.
